security_spec.violation_condition: In check_zicbo_envcfg() at target/riscv/op_helper.c:148, when env->priv < PRV_M and the menvcfg enable bit (CBZE/CBCFE/CBIE) is 0, QEMU raises RISCV_EXCP_ILLEGAL_INST for all non-M modes without inspecting env->virt_enabled. The corrected spec requires VS/VU modes to raise VirtualInstruction (RISCV_EXCP_VIRT_INSTRUCTION_FAULT) instead, so the HS-mode hypervisor can trap-and-emulate. QEMU's flat menvcfg check at line 148 fires before the virt_enabled path at line 152 is reached, causing the exception to route to M-mode with the wrong exception code, bypassing the hypervisor delegation path (medeleg[22]).
security_spec.summary: check_zicbo_envcfg raises IllegalInstruction for VS/VU modes when menvcfg enable bit is 0, but spec requires VirtualInstruction so HS-mode hypervisor can trap-and-emulate CBO instructions

findings.finding: The menvcfg check at line 148 fires for VS/VU modes (env->priv < PRV_M) before the virt_enabled path at line 152 is reached, causing QEMU to raise RISCV_EXCP_ILLEGAL_INST instead of RISCV_EXCP_VIRT_INSTRUCTION_FAULT. The sequential if structure (no else-if) means the menvcfg check at line 148 unconditionally catches all non-M modes including VS/VU, and riscv_raise_exception() longjmps out before the virt_enabled check at line 152 can execute. The corrected spec requires VS/VU modes to raise VirtualInstruction so the HS-mode hypervisor can trap-and-emulate, but QEMU routes the exception to M-mode with the wrong exception code, bypassing the hypervisor delegation path (medeleg[22] for illegal-instruction). Fix: add !env->virt_enabled guard to line 148, or restructure to use else-if matching the spec's pseudo-code.

spec_citations.excerpt: [[norm:cbo-zero_basedon_xenvcfg-CBZE]] Finally, a cbo.zero instruction executes or raises an illegal-instruction or virtual-instruction exception based on the state of the envcfg[cbze] bits: // illegal-instruction exceptions if (((priv_mode != M) && !menvcfg.CBZE) || ((priv_mode == U) && !senvcfg.CBZE)) { <raise illegal-instruction exception> } // virtual-instruction exceptions else if (((priv_mode == VS) && !henvcfg.CBZE) || ((priv_mode == VU) && !(henvcfg.CBZE && senvcfg.CBZE))) { <raise virtual-instruction exception> }

[[norm:cbo-inval]] A cbo.inval instruction executes or raises either an illegal-instruction exception or a virtual-instruction exception based on the state of the envcfg[cbie] fields: // illegal-instruction exceptions if (((priv_mode != M) && (menvcfg.CBIE == 00)) || ((priv_mode == U) && (senvcfg.CBIE == 00))) { <raise illegal-instruction exception> } // virtual-instruction exceptions else if (((priv_mode == VS) && (henvcfg.CBIE == 00)) || ((priv_mode == VU) && ((henvcfg.CBIE == 00) || (senvcfg.CBIE == 00)))) { <raise virtual-instruction exception> }

[[norm:cbo-clean_cbo-flush]] A cbo.clean or cbo.flush instruction executes or raises an illegal-instruction or virtual-instruction exception based on the state of the envcfg[cbcfe] bits: // illegal-instruction exceptions if (((priv_mode != M) && !menvcfg.CBCFE) || ((priv_mode == U) && !senvcfg.CBCFE)) { <raise illegal-instruction exception> } // virtual-instruction exceptions else if (((priv_mode == VS) && !henvcfg.CBCFE) || ((priv_mode == VU) && !(henvcfg.CBCFE && senvcfg.CBCFE))) { <raise virtual-instruction exception> }
